notes: Transcribed from SIR 2016-5083 ver. 1.1 (April 2017): equations, MEV, AVP, SEP and n from Table 4 (report pages 20-21); variable limits from Table 5 (page 23); covariance matrices [X^T Lambda^-1 X]^-1 from Table A5 of sir20165083_appendixa.xlsx. Values were double-entered (hand transcription vs. programmatic parse of the PDF text) with zero disagreements, and cross-checked against the live NSS service (Idaho = NSS region 16, citation 39). Units: model_error_variance and avp are Table 4's MEV and AVP columns, log10 units squared, copied as printed. sep_log is derived from Table 4's SEP (percent) as sqrt(ln(1 + (SEP/100)^2)) / ln(10); the report's SEM and pseudo-R2 are not stored. Intercept is log10 of the printed power-form coefficient. AEP 0.667 and 0.429 are the report's Q67 and Q43 (1.5- and 2.33-year recurrence; NSS PK66_7AEP and PK42_9AEP). Region 7: the report and NSS write the elevation term as (MINBELEV/1000)^b. The schema has no scale factor, so the term is stored as log10(MINBELEV) with the scale folded into the intercept (intercept = log10(a) - 3b), MINBELEV limits stay in feet, and the Table A5 covariance (published in the log10(MINBELEV/1000) basis) is re-expressed in the stored basis as M^T U M with M the identity plus M[Emin,intercept] = -3, which leaves every site-specific prediction variance unchanged. Region 4 is NOT included: its equations use (LC11FOREST/100 + 1)^b, i.e. log10(F/100 + 1), which none of the schema transforms (identity, log10, log10_plus1 = log10(F + 1)) can represent, and log10(F/100 + 1) is not an affine function of any of them. It needs a new transform before it can be added. PRECPRIS10 is NSS's code for the report's mean annual precipitation (Table 2 lists it as PRECIP, PRISM). NSS discrepancies found while cross-checking (NSS, not this file, is wrong): region 1_2 DRNAREA maximum is 107,000 mi2 in NSS but 10,700 in Table 5; NSS reports region 6_8's SEP percentages for region 7.
